title: Introduce tfstate-seeder module and gpu-subpool-reconciler controller for deterministic state and scheduling
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: upgrades of private clusters and GPU nodepool reshuffles exposed non-deterministic Terraform state boundaries in environments that previously used ad-hoc state files. This PR introduces a small, low-risk set of artifacts to (1) produce a deterministic, immutable seed for tfstate boundaries (tfstate-seeder module + migration helper), and (2) enforce GPU scheduling and subpool affinity in private installs via a reconciler controller (gpu-subpool-reconciler). Goals: minimize disruption during state migration, provide an opt-in statelock HA proxy pattern for on-prem S3-like backends, and surface safer defaults for GPU taints/labels so autoscaler + nodepool allocation behave predictably.

What this PR contains (high level):
- Terraform: new module modules/tfstate-seeder that computes canonical bucket/object names and an initial manifest file with sha-256 anchors for tenant-scoped state. Includes optional DynamoDB-style lock table configuration and an idempotent migration wrapper script (scripts/tfstate_migrate_seed.sh) to stitch existing state into the seeded layout.
- Installer chart additions: chart/statelock-proxy Helm chart (lightweight sidecar proxy for environments where a single DynamoDB-like lock service is unavailable; uses leader-election and S3 object lease semantics). Chart is optional and guarded behind values.enableStateLockProxy.
- Controller: controllers/gpu-subpool-reconciler (small controller in Go) that watches NodePools and Node objects and applies a tenant-scoped schedulingPolicy CRD at install time. The reconciler enforces label/taint canonicalization, migrates legacy node labels, and optionally annotates pools with stable subpool ids used by the TF modules for subnet claims.
- Docs: docs/upgrade/tfstate-seed.md explaining the migration steps, rollback guidance, and a checklist for production customers.

Migration/rollback strategy: the tfstate-seeder emits a seed manifest and provides a dry-run mode. The migration script takes two-phase approach: (1) seed-only (no write of main.tfstate) and verification of plan; (2) commit: upload canonical state object + update backend config pointer. Rollback is performed by re-pointing backend config to previous object and, if the statelock-proxy was used, by disabling leader election and waiting for leases to expire. Steps and commands are in docs/upgrade/tfstate-seed.md.

Security/IAM: the tf module scopes IAM policies to the minimal set required to create bucket/object + lock table and to read/restore the anchor manifest. The migration script performs an explicit confirmation check before writing seeds. The statelock-proxy runs with least-privilege S3/GCS credentials and includes a guidance snippet for integrating with KMS/HSM in air-gapped installs.

Testing done: unit tests for the tf module variables and template rendering; integration tests in bench/ci that run the migration script against a local MinIO cluster; controller e2e recorded in tests/e2e/gpu_reconciler_test.go using kind + mocked node annotations.

Why this is low-risk: modules are opt-in; defaults preserve current behaviour unless install-time flags are flipped. The migration helper is explicit and safe by default (dry-run required). The reconciler is additive and can be disabled via chart values.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module + unit tests
- [x] Helm chart for statelock-proxy + chart README
- [x] Controller implementation + e2e tests
- [x] Docs and migration guide
- [x] Security review and scoped IAM policy

Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative—seed manifests are immutable and named using tenant/org + cluster hash so we avoid accidental collisions. We expect follow-ups to add automation for scheduled background reconciliation of legacy labels and tighter RBAC controls for the statelock-proxy.

release_notes: Add optional tfstate-seeder module and statelock-proxy Helm chart to support deterministic state layout for private installs; introduce gpu-subpool-reconciler controller to canonicalize GPU node labels/taints and enable predictable scheduling. Opt-in behavior; migration helper included.
notes_for_ops: Before enabling seed migration in production: 1) run scripts/tfstate_migrate_seed.sh --dry-run against a snapshot; 2) ensure S3/GCS credentials have only the scoped rights listed in docs/upgrade/tfstate-seed.md; 3) if using statelock-proxy, deploy it in its own namespace with a single replica initially; 4) monitor tfstate writes and cluster autoscaler metrics for 24 hours post-migration.
